entries.test: US laws in force on August 23, 2024 would show whether external bodies had legally mandated authority over consequential AI-company decisions and their risks and benefits.
entries.note: The legal claim is assessed as of publication.
“So do I” explicitly adopts Saunders’s evaluation. Calling this prospect terrifying is a judgment, rather than empty rhetoric.

entries.test: Public records would establish whether the referenced board existed at publication and whether any subsequently established board obtained enforceable authority without a government mandate.
entries.note: This combines a historical observation with a conditional forecast. “You can bet” expresses firm confidence; “teeth” plainly means effective authority.
“Meagre” evaluates the adequacy of OpenAI’s reasons.

entries.test: Dated legislative submissions, correspondence, and public statements would establish whether OpenAI proposed SB-1047 amendments months before August 23, 2024, including a federal-law sunset provision.
entries.note: Marcus’s own concluding sentence endorses the factual allegation in Saunders’s preceding quotation.

The passage supplies no shared criterion for self-regulation “working”: honoring commitments, reducing risks, and preventing serious harm yield different tests. The opening phrase presents an asserted circumstance rather than an explicit future antecedent.

entries.test: The public record of SB-1047’s defeat and industry opposition, together with the binding AI rules remaining afterward, would establish whether consequential AI safety decisions largely remained subject to voluntary company regulation.
entries.note: SB-1047 was vetoed in September 2024, so the immediate regulatory aftermath is assessable. “In many ways” allows some binding regulation to remain.

“Our collective fates determined” does not identify a shared threshold for corporate control or the outcomes at issue. The sentence asserts a conditional prediction, but its sweeping consequence lacks a sufficiently determinate test.
